notes: System-versioned temporal proc (tranche 2). Three cursors walk change-points since initial load: BuyingGroups (excludes @InitialLoadDate 2013-01-01), CustomerCategories (excludes it too), then Customers (INCLUDES the initial load). Each change-point @ValidFrom snapshots ALL joined tables with FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF @ValidFrom, and the projected [Valid From]/[Valid To] are the CUSTOMER row's own period, so several output rows can share one [Valid From] (a lookup changed while the customer row stood still). The proc's ORDER BY [Valid From] is therefore NOT a total order -- captured with ordered=false so the canonicaliser's value-sort makes golden stable across re-captures. Seed change-points for customer 1: BuyingGroups current 2020-06-01 (archive 2013-01-01), CustomerCategories current 2020-09-01 (archive 2013-01-01), Customers current 2021-01-01 postal 98001 (archive 2013-01-01 postal 98000). BillToCustomerID=1 (self), PrimaryContactPersonID=3 (Cara Customer). resultset is transcribed verbatim from the proc's #CustomerChanges CREATE TABLE -- describe_first_result_set cannot introspect it (error 11526, uses a temp table); INSERT..EXEC fails loudly if this drifts from the proc's real output shape.

cases.name: all-changes
cases.why: Window opens BEFORE the initial load (2012-01-01), so all three cursors fire: BuyingGroups cursor at 2020-06-01, CustomerCategories cursor at 2020-09-01, Customers cursor at both 2013-01-01 (initial load, included) and 2021-01-01. Exercises every cursor and the initial-load INCLUSION on the customer arm; multiple rows share [Valid From]=2013-01-01 (the ordered=false tie case).

cases.name: initial-load-excluded
cases.why: @LastCutoff is EXACTLY 2013-01-01. The customer cursor's `c.ValidFrom > @LastCutoff` is strict, so the 2013-01-01 initial-load row drops out -- one fewer row than all-changes. Pins the exclusive lower bound and the @InitialLoadDate handling.

cases.name: buying-group-only
cases.why: Narrow window (2020-05-15, 2020-06-15] catches only the BuyingGroups change at 2020-06-01. One row, from the buying-group cursor alone -- category and customer cursors stay silent.

cases.name: category-only
cases.why: Narrow window (2020-08-15, 2020-09-15] catches only the CustomerCategories change at 2020-09-01. Isolates the category cursor.

cases.name: empty-window
cases.why: Window (2015-01-01, 2016-01-01] contains no change-point -> empty result (all three cursors yield nothing).
